properties.documentation: External id (wallet id??)
Snow customer id
User is related to "Holding mother company". Each user can get entitlement to selected "holding child companies". ONSC role "Association level admin" is not covered yet.
Foris ID (L1)
(Siebel Id - to be added within CZ SNOW d1)

We need the GetUserInfo API specification for both V2 and V4 segments (it should be identical for both) to see the link between the user and the CRM account, as well as the user's role associated with that account. We are interested in CRM accounts mapped to the Marketplace and ServiceNow. We do not expect accounts (e.g., holding company accounts) that are not mapped to either the Marketplace or ServiceNow to appear in the GetUserInfo output. If such an account is returned nonetheless, we need to find a way to ignore it during the "Account Selection" process in Service Hub.
Is a event channel provided by the Event Streaming API | Zdroj: Event Streaming API v4.0.0, https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF688-Event/TMF688-Event-v4.0.0.swagger.json
Zdroj: Federated ID v4.0, https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF691_FederatedIdentity/TMF691-FederatedIdentity-v4.0.0.swagger.json
It is also used as a "BA" – i.e., a billing account linked to a "CA" via an M:1 relationship.
Language identifier according to ISO 639-1.

properties.documentation: ServiceHub is the customer-facing digital layer for Atlas managed service visibility and support interaction.

VFID / Vodafone Identity / IDaaS is mandatory for ServiceHub access.
Tech debt: VFID-related technical debt: identity alignment and onboarding dependencies must be resolved for the target ServiceHub access model.
Verified design clarification 4 November 2026: the primary email RE: ServiceHub - DXL from Zdenek Sery dated 15 October 2026 describes SH BFF obtaining an IDaaS access token, calling DXL OAuth2 Token Exchange through APIX with that token as subject_token, APIX routing to AuthX, and AuthX validating it against IDaaS /oidc/introspect before issuing the DXL access token returned to ServiceHub. The token is used for DXL-protected API calls. The email is design evidence, not a complete versioned wire contract or implementation verification. Endpoint URL, client authentication, full parameters, scopes/audience, expiry/refresh and errors still require the Atlas contract. Reference-diagram nonce/state handling must not be promoted to existing SH behaviour or a new DXL requirement without the Group authentication design.
Primary technical verification 5 November 2026: Confluence TS - AuthX - authx-ts, section 3.2.1, last modified 4 June 2026, documents POST /OAuth2TokenExchangeGrant/v2/token. The API key used via APIX needs OAUTH2_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT and TMF691_FEDERATED_IDENTITY_ALL scopes. The form-urlencoded request includes grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, subject_token_type=urn:vodafone:params:oauth:token-type:vodafone_id, a valid subject_token and mandatory subject_token_iss identifying the issuing VFID environment. The response contains a Bearer DXL access token and TMF691-compliant user_info authorization assets; the token grants access only to the assets listed in that response. Example expiry/refresh values are not an Atlas production lifetime guarantee. This platform specification closes the relative endpoint and listed request-parameter evidence gaps, but does not prove Atlas API key configuration, environment URL, complete client authentication/error/refresh contract or deployment. Source: https://confluence-agile.oskarmobil.cz/display/DCP/TS+-+AuthX+-+authx-ts

Marketplace is used as subscription and company-product source for Atlas service visibility.
Tech debt: Technical debt: ONSC / WSC remain sources for user identities and roles, while CRM remains the source for customer data; target identity, role and customer-context alignment must be resolved.
SNOW EVE is the system of record for Atlas-relevant case / ticket lifecycle.

For the current Atlas CZ MVP, ServiceHub is a standalone portal accessible through its dedicated URL, with Vodafone ID authentication and local authorization using VFCZ DXL. ONSC/WSC portal integration, navigation handover and bidirectional customer-context propagation are outside the current MVP. Upstream ONSC/WSC user roles and customer relationships retrieved through DXL remain distinct from portal navigation. The historical requirement for both V2 and V4 portal entry paths is superseded for this MVP.
No purchase / license modification and no Service Desk access to ServiceHub on behalf of customer in MVP.

The current MVP uses an interim manual process to onboard V4 customers and users/administrators into SNOW. Automated V4 customer/admin onboarding and lifecycle propagation are outside the confirmed MVP. Customer and user presence, the selected company scope, and permissions for each supported ticket operation must be verified against the actual SNOW contract. Historical Atlas-filtered lifecycle propagation and the alternative full-V4 population are future design options, not the current MVP baseline. The implementation route, operational ownership, privacy/security acceptance and eventual removal of the interim process require explicit evidence; this revision does not assert that these conditions are complete.
properties.alias: V4 customer and admin presence in SNOW

properties.documentation:
ServiceHub requires a user-info / customer-context lookup after VFID authentication. The standard DXL/API behaviour supports V4 without the additional parameter, while V2 requires an additional parameter that causes significant performance degradation and may also affect shared WSC/ONSC channels. For Drop 1 / MVP, V2 access may need to be constrained to Atlas-relevant customers as a short-term mitigation. This protects WSC/ONSC stability but may reduce customer adoption and increase load on assisted channels. Full V2 enablement is expected in a later drop and should be owned and traced under the SNOW / ServiceNow-for-Business related delivery stream, unless another owner is formally confirmed. SNOW V2 backend readiness does not automatically imply ServiceHub V2 customer-facing visibility.
Tech debt: Strategic DXL/API optimization is required to support V2 and V4 without the additional parameter and without performance degradation. Current estimate from source material is high effort and outside MVP timeline. Ownership, funding and prioritization must be confirmed.
Review qualification 4 November 2026: retain the preceding paragraph as historical risk/mitigation context, not proof of measured degradation, an approved V2 exclusion or a quantified NFR. The directly read TMF691 specification confirms that V2 must be requested explicitly and returns root-level assets, with southbound limitations; it does not establish an Atlas performance SLO or current measurement. The Atlas rollout/role scope and any mitigation require the applicable MVP decision and accountable owner. Do not infer the target holding parent-child payload from this AS-IS API limitation.
properties.alias: V2 ServiceHub access and DXL/API performance

properties.documentation: User access to ServiceHub is possible only via Vodafone Identity / VFID. Successful VFID authentication is mandatory for ServiceHub interaction.

ServiceHub does not manage its own roles or permissions. Authorization is context-based and derived from upstream systems separately for each Customer Account. ServiceHub must not inherit access automatically across different customer entities.

VFID sub maps one-to-one to the corresponding ONSC/WSC user. Email is an attribute, not the stable identity mapping key. This identity relation is separate from the user's multiple authorized customer contexts and from the target TMF691 holding parent-child relation. According to UC005, ServiceHub automatically selects one available CRM ID and allows switching among available contexts; the initial-selection priority remains unconfirmed. Without the required role/context, general content is shown rather than granting customer-specific access. If the selected CRM ID is no longer available, the selector must be refreshed without switching to an unavailable context. Keep service eligibility, customer context, and SNOW company/user scope separate. Specific company cardinalities and holding wire payloads require the relevant contracts.
Marketplace is the source of truth for Atlas subscriptions, product status and company-product relationships.
SNOW EVE is the ticketing system for Atlas-relevant support cases. Atlas terminology refers to the customer support item as a case; lifecycle handling is managed in SNOW EVE.

The current Atlas CZ MVP uses a standalone ServiceHub access model through a dedicated URL. ONSC/WSC navigation integration and return journeys are future scope and are not prerequisites for standalone access. Vodafone ID authentication and the required VFCZ DXL authorization flow remain in scope. This statement does not exclude upstream ONSC/WSC role and relationship data.

ServiceHub derives eligible customer scope from upstream role and relationship data and enforces access within the selected authorized context. Distinguish UC005 authentication/role/context handling, UC006 Atlas service visibility using Marketplace data, and UC007/UC010/UC011 ticket operations. Missing eligible role or CRM context leads to general content, not customer-specific access. Active Atlas subscription and SNOW user/company readiness are checked where the relevant service or ticket operation requires them; SNOW presence is not a prerequisite for every item of general ServiceHub content. ServiceHub refreshes or restricts the affected context when upstream eligibility changes. This does not introduce an independent upstream identity or role-provisioning authority in ServiceHub. Exact eligible role enums, per-operation permissions and refresh/error contracts remain subject to confirmation.

Before first Atlas activation for a V4 customer, VFID / WSC existence and at least one administrator must be validated as a manual business / provisioning check unless a later detailed design explicitly confirms automated system-to-system validation or blocking. This validation does not by itself confirm automatic V4 customer/admin creation in SNOW.
V4 customer administrators may change during lifecycle by add, remove or change action. The target solution must define how those administrator lifecycle changes are reflected in SNOW.

V4 customer and administrator representation in SNOW is not yet confirmed as an implemented SNOW EVE scope item. The currently described Atlas-filtered customer/admin lifecycle model is one target option. A second decision option exists: full V4 Business customer/admin population in SNOW without filtering by active Atlas product. This alternative has data volume, lifecycle, privacy and active/passive status implications and must be explicitly decided.

properties.documentation: SREQ-CRM-01: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide customer and company context data required for ServiceHub access context resolution.
SREQ-CRM-02: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide data needed to support users linked to more than one customer entity.
SREQ-CRM-03: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide customer-entity separation data required to keep data, permissions and actions separate across unrelated customer entities.

SREQ-CRM-04: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide customer hierarchy and relationship data required for context-aware access, including child Customer Accounts, holdings and associations where applicable.
SREQ-CRM-05: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide the resolved or selected customer context used by ServiceHub for content retrieval and user actions.
SREQ-CRM-06: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide the list of Customer Accounts available for user selection when multiple Customer Accounts are associated with the user identity.
SREQ-CRM-07: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide the selected Customer Account context used by ServiceHub for all content retrieval and user actions.
SREQ-CRM-08: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel shall provide Customer Account context required before ServiceHub enables service-specific functionality.

SREQ-CRM-09: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel team shall configure the service.vodafone.com email address for Atlas product tickets created in Siebel CRM, if this assisted-ticket path is confirmed as applicable.
SREQ-CRM-10: [4.3 CRM / Siebel] CRM / Siebel team shall confirm whether Atlas / Type C products are represented in CRM and define the identification rule used by support and downstream processes.

element.name: SREQ-CRM-11 - Manage Atlas commercial lead or opportunity

properties.documentation: SREQ-ID-01: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Vodafone Identity / IDaaS shall authenticate all users via Vodafone Identity / VFID before granting access to ServiceHub.
SREQ-ID-02: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Vodafone Identity / IDaaS shall reject access to ServiceHub when VFID authentication fails.
SREQ-ID-03: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Vodafone Identity / IDaaS and Local DXL shall enforce authentication for all ServiceHub entry paths including ONSC, WSC and direct URL access.
SREQ-ID-04: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Vodafone Identity / IDaaS shall prevent anonymous access to any ServiceHub functionality.
SREQ-ID-05: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Vodafone Identity / IDaaS shall establish an authenticated session for each ServiceHub user interaction.

SREQ-ID-06: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Identity / IDaaS and local integration teams shall retrieve identity data from VFID and map it to User ID and customer context used by local systems.

SREQ-ID-07: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Local DXL shall support resolution of access context using upstream data from ONSC, WSC, CRM and Marketplace.
Review clarification 4 November 2026: preserve the Local DXL responsibility above. Vodafone Identity/IDaaS provides authentication and identity-side claims; VFCZ DXL retrieves upstream relationships, roles and CRM context; ServiceHub evaluates access to its customer-specific content. The current Book1 F166 makes this separation explicit. This clarification is a target responsibility statement, not evidence of a new AS-IS implementation or a complete token negotiation contract.

SREQ-ID-08: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Identity, ONSC and SNOW teams shall use the V2 user identity provided by ONSC to identify the user for ticketing in SNOW EVE, after the identifier is explicitly aligned with the SNOW EVE project.

SREQ-ID-09: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Identity, WSC and SNOW teams shall use the V4 user identity provided by WSC to identify the user for ticketing in SNOW EVE, after the identifier is explicitly aligned with the SNOW EVE project.

SREQ-ID-10: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Vodafone Identity / IDaaS and Local DXL teams shall enable ServiceHub SSO for V2 and V4 using CZ IDaaS and required TMF691-related local DXL changes.

SREQ-ID-11: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Provisioning / identity teams shall support manual business validation of VFID / WSC existence before first Atlas activation for V4 customer onboarding, unless detailed design confirms automated validation or blocking.

SREQ-ID-12: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Identity, WSC / Self-care and SNOW teams shall confirm the owner and source of V4 administrator lifecycle events and define how add, remove and change actions are propagated to SNOW.

SREQ-ID-13: [4.4 Vodafone Identity / IDaaS / Local DXL] Local DXL / API team shall resolve or mitigate the V2 user-info / customer-context lookup performance issue; for MVP, the team shall support the agreed mitigation and hand over full V2 enablement to the confirmed owning delivery stream.
SREQ-IVR-01: [4.7 Local IVR / Telephony] Local IVR / Telephony and Care teams shall enable or incorporate a managed services support option in Czech IVR / telephone support.
SREQ-MKP-01: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide Marketplace subscription and company-product data required for ServiceHub access context resolution.

SREQ-MKP-02: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide Atlas and ServiceHub-related subscription status for the resolved customer context before ServiceHub enables service-specific functionality.
SREQ-MKP-03: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide active Atlas subscription state for the resolved customer context.
SREQ-MKP-04: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide absence of active Atlas or other ServiceHub-related subscription for the resolved customer context.
SREQ-MKP-05: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide product data required before ServiceHub displays Atlas or other ServiceHub-related services.
SREQ-MKP-06: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide active Atlas subscription data required for ServiceHub to display Atlas service content.
SREQ-MKP-07: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect shall provide availability or error status needed by ServiceHub when Marketplace data is unavailable.

SREQ-MKP-08: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect team shall support population of CRM account number / External_Company_ID for new Marketplace customers and existing customers, either manually or by agreed batch mechanism.
SREQ-MKP-09: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect team shall include Atlas managed service charges in existing Marketplace billing files sent to Billing / Kenan.

SREQ-MKP-10: [4.2 Marketplace / AppDirect] Marketplace / AppDirect team shall provide activation state or activation event information for downstream operational processing after Atlas subscription activation.

element.name: SREQ-MKP-11 - Provide Atlas subscription lifecycle events
SREQ-MKP-FUT-01 - Handle add-subscription order initiated from ServiceHub
SREQ-MKP-FUT-02 - Handle termination request initiated from ServiceHub

properties.documentation: SREQ-PORTAL-01: [4.6 ONSC / WSC Portals] ONSC and WSC portal teams shall route all ServiceHub entry points through the authenticated VFID access flow.
SREQ-PORTAL-02: [4.6 ONSC / WSC Portals] ONSC and WSC portal teams shall provide upstream user and entry-context data required for ServiceHub access context resolution.
SREQ-PORTAL-03: [4.6 ONSC / WSC Portals] Local portal systems may restrict navigation to the ServiceHub entry point based on subscription eligibility in local entry channels.

element.name: SREQ-PORTAL-04 - Expose ServiceHub entry point in ONSC
SREQ-PORTAL-05 - Expose ServiceHub entry point in WSC
SREQ-PORTAL-06 - Keep ServiceHub entry behaviour consistent across channels

properties.documentation: SREQ-SH-01: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall evaluate authorization using upstream role data and customer context provided by Self-care systems.
SREQ-SH-02: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall not maintain its own role model and shall rely on upstream systems for role and permission evaluation.
SREQ-SH-03: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall deny access for V4 users with role End User.
SREQ-SH-04: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall deny access for V4 users with role Billing Account User.
SREQ-SH-05: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow access for V4 users with role Administrator within the valid company/customer context.
SREQ-SH-06: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall deny access for V2 users with role End User.
SREQ-SH-07: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall deny access for V2 users with role End User Admin.
SREQ-SH-08: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow access for V2 users with role Group Administrator within the valid customer context.
SREQ-SH-09: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow access for V2 users with role Administrator within the valid customer context.
SREQ-SH-10: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow access for V2 users with role Association Administrator within the valid customer context.
SREQ-SH-11: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall evaluate authorization in the context of a specific User ID and the active customer entity.
SREQ-SH-12: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall not inherit access implicitly across different customer entities under the same VFID.
SREQ-SH-13: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display only data associated with the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SH-14: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow only actions permitted within the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SH-15: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall apply access restrictions based on upstream role data.
SREQ-SH-16: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall use only the resolved or actively selected customer context for content retrieval and user actions.
SREQ-SH-17: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow the user to select a Customer Account when multiple Customer Accounts are associated with the user identity.
SREQ-SH-18: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall use only the resolved or actively selected Customer Account as the context for all content retrieval and user actions.
SREQ-SH-19: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall require a Customer Account to be selected before enabling access to service-specific functionality when multiple Customer Accounts are available.
SREQ-SH-20: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall enable service-specific functionality only when an active Atlas subscription exists in Marketplace for the resolved customer context.

SREQ-SH-21: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall not enable service-specific functionality when no active Atlas or other ServiceHub-related subscription exists in Marketplace for the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SH-22: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display Atlas service content when an active Atlas subscription exists for the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SH-23: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display a defined no-product page or defined message when no active Atlas subscription exists for the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SH-24: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display a defined empty state when no services are available for the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SH-25: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display a defined error state when Marketplace data is unavailable.
SREQ-SH-26: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall provide clear user messaging for no-product, empty and error states.
SREQ-SH-27: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display all tickets associated with the resolved customer context to authorized users onboarded for that customer context.
SREQ-SH-28: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall not limit ticket visibility only to tickets created by the current user.
SREQ-SH-29: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall create tickets under the identity of the current authenticated user.
SREQ-SH-30: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall prevent ticket creation when the current user is not onboarded in SNOW EVE.
SREQ-SH-31: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall allow access to ServiceHub even when the current user is not onboarded in SNOW EVE.
SREQ-SH-32: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall restrict ticket-related functionality when the current user is not onboarded in SNOW EVE.
SREQ-SH-33: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall disable ticket-related functionality when SNOW EVE data is unavailable.
SREQ-SH-34: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall display a defined degraded state when SNOW EVE data is unavailable.
SREQ-SH-35: [4.1 ServiceHub] ServiceHub shall dynamically update visible content and available actions when identity, role, customer context or subscription status changes.

element.name: SREQ-SH-36 - Expose ServiceHub entry point from local digital channels
SREQ-SH-37 - Display generic ServiceHub customer-facing content
SREQ-SH-38 - Guide customer to assisted support channel

SREQ-SH-42 - Apply V2 ServiceHub access mitigation

SREQ-SH-FUT-02 - Support Atlas subscription add request
SREQ-SH-FUT-03 - Support Atlas subscription termination request

properties.documentation: SREQ-SNOW-01: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall provide ticket data to ServiceHub based on the resolved customer context.
SREQ-SNOW-02: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall provide all tickets associated with the resolved customer context to ServiceHub for authorized users onboarded for that customer context.
SREQ-SNOW-03: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall support ticket retrieval by resolved customer context and shall not restrict returned tickets only to tickets created by the current user.
SREQ-SNOW-04: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall accept ticket creation under the identity of the current authenticated user.
SREQ-SNOW-05: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall expose user onboarding status required to prevent ticket creation when the current user is not onboarded in SNOW EVE.
SREQ-SNOW-06: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall expose onboarding status without blocking non-ticket ServiceHub access when the current user is not onboarded in SNOW EVE.
SREQ-SNOW-07: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall provide onboarding status required by ServiceHub to restrict ticket-related functionality when the current user is not onboarded in SNOW EVE.
SREQ-SNOW-08: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall align the V2 ONSC user identifier used for ticketing before implementation.
SREQ-SNOW-09: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall align the V4 WSC user identifier used for ticketing before implementation.
SREQ-SNOW-10: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall expose availability state required by ServiceHub to disable ticket-related functionality when SNOW EVE data is unavailable.
SREQ-SNOW-11: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE shall expose degraded-state information required by ServiceHub when SNOW EVE data is unavailable.
SREQ-SNOW-12: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE team shall support triage, resolution, escalation and Group feedback handling for Atlas-related cases.

SREQ-SNOW-13: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW EVE / operations teams shall support onboarding workflow, subscription availability handling and mismatch investigation where applicable; additional-user profile creation in SNOW shall remain traceable through the agreed Atlas service design process.

SREQ-SNOW-14: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW project / SNOW EVE team shall ensure that each V4 customer with an active Atlas product exists in SNOW where ServiceHub ticketing is required, according to the selected V4 onboarding model and confirmed ownership.

SREQ-SNOW-15: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW project / SNOW EVE team shall ensure that administrators of V4 customers with active Atlas products exist in SNOW where they are expected to create, view or close Atlas-related tickets via ServiceHub, after trigger, mapping and ownership are agreed.

SREQ-SNOW-16: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW project / SNOW EVE team shall reflect administrator lifecycle changes in SNOW and keep administrator state aligned with WSC / Self-care according to the confirmed lifecycle owner and propagation mechanism.

SREQ-SNOW-17: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW project / SNOW EVE team shall align customer and administrator active presence in SNOW with Atlas product lifecycle and prevent customer/admin accounts from remaining active for Atlas service management after termination of the last Atlas product.

SREQ-SNOW-18: [4.5 SNOW EVE] SNOW project, data protection and architecture teams shall define and apply personal data protection controls for customer and administrator data propagated to or maintained in SNOW, including lifecycle end, active/passive status, retention and the full V4 population alternative.
